newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Sept open unemployment rises to 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Sept open unemployment rises to 5.5 pct.

text.p: Mexico's open, or base, unemployment rate rose to 5.5 percent during September, compared with 5.3 percent in August according to a preliminary estimate, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said on Thursday.
INEGI said in a statement the jobless rate compared with 7.3 percent open unemployment during September of last year.

For the third quarter of 1996, open unemployment was 5.5 percent, a slight improvement from 5.6 percent in the second quarter of this year and a marked improvement from 7.4 percent in the third quarter of 1995, INEGI said.
The report said open unemployment was 5.8 percent in July and 5.3 percent in August. The September figure of 5.5 percent is subject to later revision.
"It should be noted that generally, because of seasonal factors, the figure for September each year is slightly higher than that of August," INEGI said.
The average amount of time the unemployed took to find a job in the third quarter this year fell to 5.6 weeks, down from 6.2 weeks in the third quarter last year.
INEGI defines open unemployment as members of the workforce older than 12 who have searched for work, but have not worked more than one hour a week during a month.

The Rate of General Pressure, which measures those in work looking for a new job as well as open unemployment, was 8.6 percent in the third quarter of this year compared with 11.5 percent in the same period last year.

The Rate of Partial Joblessness and Unemployment, which includes open unemployment and those who have worked less than 35 hours a week due to market conditions, fell to 7.3 percent in Q3 1996 from 9.9 percent in the same period last year.

The Alternative Open Unemployment Rate, which includes open unemployment, as well as those who have given up looking for work, fell to 6.4 percent in the third quarter this year against 9.9 percent in the third quarter last year.
